# Frozen graph compatibility inputs

These exact JSON bytes are inputs to the IsOS `1.0.0` compatibility reader tests. The safe fixture is the JSON form of the current `templates/generic-graph.toml` starter: it contains `eos.dispatcher.control@v1.0` and the bounded role-selected `isos.process.component@v1.1` nodes. Keep the bytes stable when testing original-byte revisions; a deliberate fixture update must also update the SHA-256 values below. None is a new deployment template.

## Exact current identity inventory

The current graph envelope is `1.0.0`. The EOS built-in registry admits these exact type IDs: `eos.hardware.camera@v1.0`, `eos.hardware.base@v1.0`, `eos.hardware.manipulator@v1.0`, `eos.dispatcher.control@v1.0`, `eos.dispatcher.primitive_base@v1.0`, `eos.dispatcher.primitive_manipulator@v1.0`, `eos.control.manual@v1.0`, `eos.control.primitive@v1.0`, `eos.control.skill@v1.0`, `eos.interface.camera_gate@v1.0`, `eos.process.backend@v1.0`, `egia.common.source@v1.0`, `egia.common.context@v1.0`, `egia.common.planner@v1.0`, `egia.common.guard@v1.0`, `isos.process.component@v1.0`, `isos.process.component@v1.1`, `isos.ui.vision@v1.0`, and `isosui.system.vision@v1.0`. The MuJoCo package contributes `eos.process.mujoco@v1.0` and may carry legacy `eos.hardware.mujoco_camera@v1.0`, `eos.hardware.mujoco_base@v1.0`, and `eos.hardware.mujoco_manipulator@v1.0`. Registration is exact: other suffixes or names are not implicitly compatible. The four `egia.common` identities and `eos.control.skill@v1.0` remain design or historical compatibility only; they acquire no new execution route. IsOS rejects `isos.process.component@v1.0` and `eos.process.backend@v1.0` before process launch even though their identities remain inspectable.

IsOS verifies contribution metadata in `src/domain/release.rs`, writes the package sidecar in `src/domain/packages.rs`, uses its exact type IDs in node-set composition, merges the verified catalog in `src/runtime/process.rs`, passes `--node-types` to EOS validation and child launch, and includes exact package references in core setup. EGIA receives its graph subtree through setup; IsosUI reads IsOS's aggregated node-type catalog. Neither client loads sidecar files directly.

For an absent graph or an unapplied starter without `core-setup/launch-inputs.json`, IsOS still admits the first edited `1.0.0` Apply in this reader slice. It uses existing canonical JSON serialization and computes the revision from the bytes actually written. Once an applied snapshot exists, a changed legacy graph requires explicit migration; a structurally identical Apply preserves its original bytes and revision. G03 migration, the `0.1.0` writer, and the separate G02 read-only inspection projection are implemented. A known-unmapped legacy graph is read-only and fails Validate, Apply, setup, Run, Restart and readiness at its exact path.

## G03 migration fixtures — implemented

[`migration_mapping.json`](migration_mapping.json) fixes every allowed old-to-new type pair, exact safe pass-through identity, conditional MuJoCo package mapping, and forbidden automatic conversion. [`migration_expected_0_1_0.json`](migration_expected_0_1_0.json) is the **semantic** expected result of migrating `legacy_1_0_0.json`: `/version`, the one EOS dispatcher type, and three IsOS role-selected component types change; all other JSON fields and values remain identical. Its file SHA-256 is `825d667d31c455844be7f22b565e0ab6b14b44aeb7ce4861a704ffd028081df1`; this is both the fixture integrity check and proposed revision under the canonical writer specified in the graph contract. The source remains `7a8daee6b7db9105f5483506ffc1743625b63089710dfbf936622329c471016b` and must remain byte-for-byte unchanged after preview, stale compare, unsafe-node rejection, missing owner reader, failed render, or filesystem publish failure.

Implementation tests should compare the parsed migrated value with this fixture, then verify its own canonical output digest. They should add one package-backed graph with nested `package` and `adapter.package` exact pins, settings, references, edges, and permitted extension fields; assert these values survive preview and commit. A linked package fingerprint change, unknown field, missing target contribution, or stale preview digest must fail at a precise path with no saved-byte or active-revision change. A successful commit changes the saved revision but keeps `active_revision` until Restart. The source fixture's IsOS `component@v1.1` nodes exercise the IsOS `@v0.1` contribution and EOS reader feature at the G03 migration gate.

For the G03 new-writer transition, a missing graph GET and a fresh Init produce the same `0.1.0` starter node identities as `migration_expected_0_1_0.json`; existing legacy saved bytes must remain unchanged on Init. A first new-version PUT uses empty `revision`, and a later changed PUT or CLI Apply uses the exact saved digest. A new-version fixture run must create `data/generated/default/<saved-revision>/core-setup/launch-inputs.json` and `eos/graph.json`, validate the manifest, and pass the latter to EOS runtime and config-server as their effective `--profile` without changing the source graph's `settings.args`. A legacy run still uses only the flat `data/generated/default/core-setup/launch-inputs.json`. The test must reject a 0.1 graph with any cross-core edge/reference before G06, and must validate `isos.process.component@v0.1` in IsOS rather than asking EOS whole-profile validation to own it. More than 256 mapped changes rejects at `/changes`; a graph-parent fsync failure after rename is an uncertain outcome resolved by rereading the saved digest.

## G02 inspection projection — implemented

The two new fixtures above freeze a second read view without changing G03 migration input. `legacy_1_0_0.json` and `legacy_1_0_0_whitespace.json` must produce equal `legacy_projection.graph`, `mappings`, `defaults`, and `display_descriptions` values, while each `source_revision` equals its distinct raw-byte SHA above. The four mapped nodes are one EOS dispatcher and three IsOS role-selected components; the nine-pair G03 table and four EGIA pass-through identities remain the sole mapping authority. The optional-default fixture must produce the same raw-byte SHA before and after GET, Validate, and structurally identical no-op Apply. `future_2_0_0.json`, `unknown_type_1_0_0.json`, `unsafe_component_1_0_0.json`, and `legacy_unmapped_1_0_0.json` yield no partial projection. GET still exposes syntactically valid raw JSON and the first exact-path diagnostic; the unsafe fixture keeps `unsafe_process_node` precedence. A changed applied legacy PUT remains `migration_required`; a completely mapped unapplied starter retains the first edited Apply exception. Tests should also prove that passing projection JSON as a PUT value cannot silently replace saved bytes or candidate type IDs.
